candidates.spoken: Why one teaspoon of neutron star would explode.
What If You Held a Teaspoon of Neutron Star?
Neutron stars pack 1.4 Suns into about 10 kilometres.
Outside the star, that matter wouldn't stay compressed.
A teaspoon of neutron-star matter appeared on Earth.
So the teaspoon isn't a weight.
Squeeze Earth that hard, and it fits in 305 metres.
A neutron-star teaspoon wouldn't just be heavy.
It would not all happen at once.
Freed from crushing gravity, it would expand violently.
